Quite a few setups people show off include MPD. But you need the server, and a client which doesn't usually look very nice. It appears easier to use a complete media management solution like Exaile or Audacious. Why do people like MPD?

Because you can use multiple clients to work with the same playback engine.

There are command line clients that make it easy to script stuff or attach keybindings, you can control MPD remotely from other devices running clients and things like that.

You can even restart X without interrupting your music.

It's been a while since I used it but I liked: https://gmpclient.org

EDIT: actually I was thinking of Sonata: http://mpd.wikia.com/wiki/Client:Sonata

Plus, MPD+Cantata is more lightweight than Clementine by ~19MB.

Most of all: On a multi-user system you can have a common playlist for all users to share. Someone didn't log out and left their music running? No problem. Want to append a track of yours while someone else's is playing? Easy.

And you can install it on a server and control the music in your home from your desktop, laptop, phone, what have you.

I'm reasonably computer literate - I've used Linux for 20 years, done countless Arch installs on many different desktops and laptops. I've used other server type applications, web, DB, etc. But I have not ONCE been able to get MPD to work right. Reading through the docs, it seems it should be straight forward enough. But nope, never works. I just use Cmus if I need a CLI music player.
